hook_text: Every second, about four babies are born somewhere on Earth, and about two people die. Do the maths.
clip_script: More births than deaths means the world keeps growing: past eight billion people now. But how do we compare a giant country with a tiny one? Per thousand. Take a town of fifty thousand. A thousand babies born this year? That's a birth rate of twenty per thousand. Four hundred deaths? A death rate of eight. Subtract: twelve per thousand. Divide by ten: one point two percent growth a year. Niger grows over three percent a year and doubles in under twenty-five years. South Africa grows about one percent. Japan? More deaths than births. It's shrinking. Same simple equation, three completely different futures.
visual_style: A whiteboard counter of babies and gravestones ticking; a town with 50 000 written on it; the sum 20 minus 8 equals 12 writing itself; three country silhouettes with arrows up fast, up slowly and down.
pacing: Number hook, a fast worked example, a dramatic comparison.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and calculate population growth yourself.
